facts.fact: Google turned off third-party cookies for 30 million Chrome users in early January, which the page says was about 1% of Chrome's total user base.
facts.quote: turned off cookies for 30 million Chrome users

facts.fact: Google has promised to turn off third-party cookies completely in Chrome by 2025, after delaying the change for a third time.
facts.quote: promise to turn off 3rd-party cookies completely by 2025

facts.fact: According to HubSpot, less than half of marketers have a plan in place for cookie-free targeting.
facts.quote: less than half of marketers have a plan in place for cookie-free targeting

facts.fact: In the same Econsultancy survey, only 8% of respondents felt fully prepared for the cookieless future.
facts.quote: only 8% felt “fully prepared” for the cookieless future

facts.fact: According to Digiday, 78% of publishers believe removing third-party cookies will make their audience data more valuable.
facts.quote: 78% of publishers believe removing third-party cookies will make their audience data “more valuable”

facts.fact: In an ID5 survey, 25% of respondents believe 1st-party universal identifiers are the most viable and scalable solution for replacing third-party cookies.
facts.quote: believe that 1st-party universal identifiers are the most viable and scalable solution for replacing 3rd-party cookies

facts.fact: According to Digiday, only 9% of publishers have a complete plan for the end of third-party cookies.
facts.quote: says only 9% of publishers have a complete plan for the end of 3rd-party cookies

facts.fact: Proximic's 2024 State of Programmatic Report found that 78% of advertisers planned to increase or continue relying on contextual targeting in a post-cookie environment.
facts.quote: found that 78% of advertisers planned to increase or continue relying on contextual targeting to target ads in a post-cookie environment

facts.fact: Authenticated targeting occurs when an advertiser gains explicit consent from a user, often through a pop-up, login screen, or sign-up form, to use their data for advertising.
facts.quote: gains explicit consent from a user—often through a pop-up, login screen, or sign-up form
